package_info.package_name: N/A (RepoJacking is a technique, not a specific package)
package_info.package_manager: GitHub (affecting downstream: Go, Swift, Packagist, etc.)
package_info.package_versions: All versions of packages relying on vulnerable GitHub repository namespaces
package_info.why_malicious: The attack enables an adversary to take over a previously legitimate repository namespace after a username rename, allowing them to serve malicious code to all downstream consumers who rely on the original repository URL. This can poison the software supply chain at scale.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attacker creates a repository with the same name as a popular retired repository under a reclaimed username, then pushes malicious code (e.g., backdoored source, malicious workflow, or package manager payload).
malicious_snippets.code_language: varies (Go, PHP, Swift, JavaScript, YAML, etc.)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When users or automated systems fetch or install code from the hijacked repository URL, they receive attacker-controlled (potentially malicious) code instead of the original trusted code.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Hijacking a trusted namespace to serve new, attacker-controlled code is a classic supply chain attack vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior expects repository URLs to remain under the control of the original maintainer or be permanently retired. RepoJacking breaks this trust model.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate repository transfers or username changes, but not with the intent to deceive or serve malicious code.
key_indicators: Repository namespace previously belonged to a popular project
Repository content changes drastically after takeover
Malicious payloads or suspicious workflow files appear

attack_chain.action: Attacker monitors for popular repositories whose owners have renamed their usernames, leaving the old username available.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can register the old username.

attack_chain.action: Attacker registers the old username and creates a repository with the same name as the original (retired) repository.
attack_chain.leads_to: Repository namespace is now under attacker control.

attack_chain.action: Attacker pushes malicious code or workflows to the hijacked repository.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is served to all consumers using the original repository URL.

attack_chain.action: Downstream users or automated systems (e.g., package managers, CI/CD) fetch or install code from the hijacked repository, unknowingly executing attacker-supplied code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential compromise of developer systems, CI/CD pipelines, or production environments.

behavioral_signatures: Repository namespace previously associated with a popular project is suddenly re-registered by a new account
Drastic changes in repository content or commit history after a username rename
New repository owner pushes code with suspicious or malicious payloads
Unexpected changes in GitHub Actions workflows or package manager manifests
file_indicators: Repository files with backdoors, credential stealers, or obfuscated code
New or modified .github/workflows/* files with suspicious automation
network_indicators: Downstream systems making requests to attacker-controlled infrastructure after updating dependencies
Unexpected external network connections initiated by newly fetched code
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for repository namespace re-registrations following username renames, especially for popular projects. Alert on drastic changes in repository content or commit history. Scan for suspicious or malicious code in newly created repositories with previously retired namespaces. Use dependency management tools to pin to specific commit hashes or use the new, correct repository URLs rather than relying on username-based URLs.
